reported.title: 16-bit millis wrap breaks scheduling
reported.description: tickNow() truncates millis() to uint16_t and compares with >=, so every ~65.5 s the schedule breaks: after wrap, now is small while nextRunAt/stopRunAt are large, causing runs to be skipped or stuck until the timers wrap again. Use unsigned long and subtraction-based comparisons.

reported.title: Hold switch not debounced
reported.description: held() reads D3 directly each loop with no debounce, so contact bounce on the switch can toggle D6 rapidly, violating the max-2-transitions-per-5s rule and chattering the relay.

reported.title: Relay can toggle more than twice per 5 s window
reported.description: drive() recomputes on every loop from running && !held(); a bouncing or briefly released hold switch can flip D6 many times within a 5 s window, exceeding the stated 2-transition limit.

truth.description: The 16-bit clock is compared with absolute deadlines, so the schedule breaks whenever the clock wraps, every 65.5 s of uptime

truth_for_judge.description: The 16-bit clock is compared with absolute deadlines, so the schedule breaks whenever the clock wraps, every 65.5 s of uptime

exposing_checks.behaviour: serial lines matching '^mix \\d+$' every 5000 ms (A run starts every 5 s)
D6 must not toggle more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window (Mixer switching rate)

judge_input.spec:
- Mixer relay on D6; hold switch on D3 with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Run the mixer (D6 HIGH) for 2000 ms out of every 5000 ms, the first run starting 5000 ms after power-up.
- Print `mix <n>` when each run starts, once per 5000 ms ±250 ms.
- While D3 is held LOW, keep D6 LOW. The runs are still counted and printed.
- The mixer must not change state more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window.
